messages.author: 31125dd089bdaf48
messages.subject: multi-factorial barcharts with ggplot2?
parts:
Hello together,

I'm a gplot2-newbie and would like to create some multi-factorial
barcharts. The plot I've in mind is inspired by the way Excel allows
to do multi-factorial barcharts. I've uploaded an example here:
http://imageshare.web.id/images/h40k7ujes2wpl8eo2xzw.png
As you can see I have a many different factors (in fact the example
shows just a subset of them) which I would like to include into a
single plot. With excel this is possible, but I would like to use R
instead if possible.

I've played around with the different possibilities of faceting of
ggplot2 but couldn't produce a plot which looks similar to the one of
my example. My main concern is that the factor-structure is much more
obvious in the Excel compared to the faceted results generated by
ggplot2. This is because of the layered displaying in Excel (one row
per factor), and the comma-separation of factor-levels in the subplots
of ggplot2 when using faceting like
facet_grid(. ~ position + treatment + concentration).

Is it possible to reproduce my example with ggplot2? If not, are you
aware of any other R-library which would allow such multi-factorial
plots?

The only example I'm aware of has been posted here:
http://onertipaday.blogspot.com/2007/05/make-many-barplot-into-one-plot.html
However, the provided solution does not generalizes to other
situations.

Any idea or suggestion is cordially welcome. :-)

Best, Holger Brandl

but it isn't quite there yet, because facet_wrap isn't intelligent
enough to know how to combine factor levels. It's something I hope to
work on later this summer.

Hadley
